title: GPU downtime orchestration matrix — May 2026
content:
Purpose:
This doc is an operational playbook + orchestration matrix for planned GPU maintenance that requires capacity drains (driver upgrades, firmware updates, and kernel/driver rolling). The goal is to maintain SLAs for hosted API and Dedicated customers while performing necessary fleet maintenance with controlled risk.

Scope and context:
- Scope: All production GPU clusters across regions (us-west1, us-east4, eu-west1, asia-east1). Includes both shared-hosted pools and Dedicated reserved pools used by customer tenants.
- Out of scope: on-prem private deployments (separate private-runbook).
- Target outage type: rolling drain of physical GPU hosts (evict pods/processes, migrate KV caches, update drivers, reboot host as needed).

High-level constraints / objectives:
- Maintain 99.9% regional availability during maintenance windows for critical routes.
- No more than 10% of capacity drained in any 30-min rolling window for a single region unless escalation approved.
- Canary first: validate driver + runtime on a small canary set for at least 45 minutes before broad rollout.
- Use hot-standby and burst pools where possible to soak traffic.

Planned maintenance windows (default, local times are shown; scheduling cadence adaptive by region load):
- us-west1: Tue 02:00–06:00 PDT (09:00–13:00 UTC)
- us-east4: Wed 01:00–05:00 EDT (05:00–09:00 UTC)
- eu-west1: Thu 03:00–07:00 CEST (01:00–05:00 UTC)
- asia-east1: Mon 00:00–04:00 CST (16:00–20:00 UTC previous day)
Notes: windows chosen to align with local low-traffic periods. If regional utilization > 65% in the 72h preceding window, automatically shift to next available low-traffic window and notify stakeholders.

Orchestration matrix (textual):
- us-west1 | drain-order: rack-by-rack (east->west) | max-simultaneous-drain: 6% region capacity | prewarm: 8 gpus warm nodes | canary-nodes: 2 hosts (4 GPUs) | rollback budget: 30m per rack
- us-east4 | drain-order: AZ prioritization (a->b->c) | max-simultaneous-drain: 8% region capacity | prewarm: 10 gpus warm nodes | canary-nodes: 2 hosts (4 GPUs) | rollback budget: 40m per AZ
- eu-west1 | drain-order: alternating racks across AZs | max-simultaneous-drain: 5% region capacity | prewarm: 6 gpus warm nodes | canary-nodes: 1 host (2 GPUs) | rollback budget: 25m per rack
- asia-east1 | drain-order: small-batch drains (1 host at a time) | max-simultaneous-drain: 4% region capacity | prewarm: 4 gpus warm nodes | canary-nodes: 1 host | rollback budget: 20m

Pre-maintenance checks (to be completed 2–6 hours before window):
- Verify baseline metrics: regional p95 latency, token/sec, queue length. Screenshot & attach to JIRA ticket.
- Confirm spare capacity: free_gpus_percent >= 12% OR available burst pool >= expected drain volume + 5%.
- Validate health of autoscaler and routing (smoke request through routing layer).
- Confirm backups of KV caches and that cache rehydration TTLs are set to 1h for the maintenance period.
- Ensure support rotation: on-call SRE, infra lead, and concierge runbook owner are present in the maintenance Slack channel.

Runbook (step-by-step):
1) Canary stage (0–60m):
   - Select canary hosts (see matrix). Label hosts with `maintenance=canary` and drain workloads with command: `infractl drain-host --id HOST --mode graceful --notify-routing`.
   - Apply driver package to canary: `infractl host-update --id HOST --driver vX.Y.Z --reboot-if-needed`
   - Run smoke tests against canary: perf_sanity.sh (p95 < baseline * 1.15; token/sec degradation < 10%).
   - Run eval prompts set `driver-canary-smoke` (5 deterministic prompts per model) — compare outputs for regressions.
   - If failure -> rollback: `infractl host-rollback --id HOST` and escalate to on-call.

2) Bulk drain (iterative by matrix):
   - For each rack/AZ in order: mark hosts for drain, wait for workload migration completion metric (active_gpus_on_host == 0), then perform driver update.
   - Maintain drain concurrency cap (see matrix). Adjust concurrency down if p95 rises > 20% or queued requests increase > 25%.
   - Command sequence: `infractl mark-drain HOST -> infractl migrate-workloads HOST -> infractl host-update HOST -> infractl health-check HOST`

3) Post-update validation (after each host completes):
   - Run model-level smoke tests on a small traffic shadow; check latency/throughput and correctness signatures.
   - Confirm KV cache warmup: cache_hit_rate returns to >= baseline within 15 minutes.
   - Check GPU-level metrics: GPU utilization, temperature, ECC errors. Any new ECC or driver error -> stop rollout and escalate.

Rollback and emergency cutover:
- Criteria to stop and rollback region: sustained p95 degradation > 30% for > 15 minutes OR error-rate increase > 3x baseline for > 10 minutes OR any critical Dedicated-customer SLA breach.
- Rollback command: `infractl host-rollback --id HOST` (reverts driver and reboots). For bulk rollback, use `infractl fleet-rollback --region REGION --max-parallel 4` and pause further drains.
- Escalation path: on-call -> infra leads -> eng-ops director -> product-critical contacts (list in ticket).

Capacity management heuristics and fallback routing:
- If free_gpus_percent dips < 8% during maintenance, automatically route new low-priority jobs to batch queue and apply admission control to non-critical tenants.
- Hot-standby: maintain a pool of prewarmed hosts (labels: prewarm=true) equal to 6% region capacity; these are not used for Dedicated workloads without explicit permission.
- Smart routing: routing policy can failover models to lower-cost variants (quantized) when latency SLOs are still met. This is orchestrated by `routerctl route-fallback --policy maintenance-safe`.

Driver upgrade specifics and gotchas:
- Upgrade order: driver -> CUDA -> libcudnn -> tensorlib builds. Always verify ABI compatibility for the currently pinned model runtimes.
- For quantized models (int8/int4 paths), rebuild and smoke test kernel paths if driver ABI changes. Add build flag: `-DQUANT_PATH=ON` during packaging step.
- Known-risk drivers: avoid vX.Y.1 until community fix for kernel-handshake (tracked in JIRA-DRIVER-99).

Testing matrix for canary and validation (examples):
- Perf: p50/p95/p99 for generation endpoint (baseline capture inside JIRA-INF-2148).
- Correctness: run eval set `maintenance-eval-v2` (20 prompts across embeddings/generation/rerank).
- Stress: run 1.2x expected peak token/sec for 5 minutes and ensure no OOMs.

Communication templates (Slack snippets):
- Pre-window (2h): "[MAINT] GPU maintenance planned in us-west1 at Tue 02:00 PDT. Canary start at 02:15. Expect rolling drains; we will notify on progress. Ticket: JIRA-INF-2148"
- During window (start of rack): "[MAINT] Draining rack r12 (us-west1). Targets: 6% cap. Canary validated. ETA per rack: ~14m. Watch grafana dashboard: /d/ops/gpu-capacity-overview"
- Post-window: "[MAINT] Maintenance complete for us-west1. Post-checks passing. See postmortem: <link>"

Observable checklist (metrics to watch during maintenance):
- Regional p95 latency (generation endpoints)
- Regional error rate (4xx/5xx) and Dedicated-client error spikes
- Queue depth and pending token backlog
- free_gpus_percent and hot-standby utilization
- KV cache hit rate and rehydration time
- GPU ECC and driver errors

After-action & signoffs:
- Each region run must end with a short AAR note in JIRA ticket: what succeeded, what failed, learned actions, and follow-ups (owner + due date).
- Required signoff: infra lead, SRE on-call, product ops for customer-impacting changes.

Open questions / decisions to capture before execution:
- Confirm whether Dedicated-reserved pools must be excluded by default or allowed to be drained with explicit tenant opt-in. (Decision needed: infra-policy-2026-05-01)
- Approve dynamic concurrency lowering threshold (default p95+20%).

Appendix: quick commands & shortcuts:
- Drain host: `infractl drain-host --id HOST`
- Force migrate: `infractl migrate-workloads --from HOST --to HOST2`
- Update host driver: `infractl host-update --id HOST --driver vX.Y.Z`
- Rollback host: `infractl host-rollback --id HOST`
- Fleet rollback (regional): `infractl fleet-rollback --region us-west1 --max-parallel 4`

Contact list (owners):
- Runbook owner: Priya Menon
- Infra lead: Evan Liu
- SRE on-call rotation: see PagerDuty schedule (link in ticket)
- Concierge ops: Marina Gomez, Samir O'Connor

Notes to reviewers (internal):
- This draft prefers conservative concurrency caps and explicit canary windows. Suggest a dry-run in a non-prod cluster next week (ticket: JIRA-DRYRUN-21).
- If approved, schedule region-by-region executions over the next 3 weeks and attach dedicated customer notification list for each region.

(End of document)
